what: per-token log-probabilities of the MODEL-AUTHOR implementation on the 32 hidden sequences

reference.implementation: inference/model.py from the checkpoint deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash at revision 60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1
reference.checkpoint: converted with the author's own inference/convert.py --n-experts 256 --model-parallel 4, expert_dtype unset so the native FP4 experts are kept and wo_a is dequantised to bf16 (98 s, 157 GB)
reference.dependencies: torch 2.11.0+cu130, tilelang 0.1.8 and transformers 5.6.0 from the task image; fast_hadamard_transform 1.1.0 built from github.com/Dao-AILab/fast-hadamard-transform against that torch (the PyPI sdist ships no csrc/ and its wheel 404s for this torch/CUDA/Python)
reference.patch: the one patched line: ParallelHead.get_logits returns F.linear(x.float(), self.weight) instead of F.linear(x[:, -1].float(), self.weight), so the head yields every position instead of the last; the all-gather in ParallelHead.forward already handles the extra dimension
reference.procedure: one prefill per sequence, model.forward(tokens[:, :-1], 0), then log_softmax in float32 and logp[t] = log P(tokens[t+1] | tokens[:t+1])

sequences.note: fixed public-domain text from inside the image; never generated by either implementation. The ids are the hidden material; the sources and offsets make the draw reproducible.

statistic: k3 = mean over positions of exp(r) - 1 - r with r = ref - served; the node value is the median over sequences. On teacher-forced tokens this is a non-negative log-ratio discrepancy, not an unbiased KL estimate.
rounding: ref_logprobs are rounded to 6 decimals; the error that introduces in r is below 1e-6, four orders of magnitude under the measured medians.
